content.text:
My searches are exhausted and consistent. Let me record the finding.

**Investigation summary:**
- Planner candidates `p0284` / `p0291` are a **no-recourse against individuals** clause and an **Indemnified Person** indemnity — neither imposes any hiring or solicitation restriction.
- `solicit`, `no-hire`, `induce`, `hire`, `personnel/recruit/staff`, `non-compete/restrictive covenant` → **zero hits** document-wide.
- `employee` / `employ` → only recourse limitations (p0244, p0284), the Indemnified Person definition (p0291), ERISA definitions (p0649, p0651, p0740) and the Independent Manager definition (p0770). None is a restrictive covenant.
- Section list confirms this is a securitization Transfer and Servicing Agreement; even Article VII (Successor Servicer transition), the usual home for employee-poaching restrictions, contains no `employee` hit.

This satisfies the **preferred** position outright. Absence of a non-solicit benefits our party, so no redline is warranted — "missing" is the wrong status here because this rule's preferred outcome *is* the absence of the clause.

input.quote: No Person will have recourse, directly or indirectly, to any member, manager, officer, director, employee or agent of the Servicer for the Servicer's obligations or the Marketing Agent for the Marketing Agent's obligations, as applicable, under this Agreement.
input.rationale:
The Agreement contains no non-solicitation, no-hire, or anti-poaching covenant binding the Issuer or Depositor (our parties), and none binding Cellco either. Targeted searches for "solicit", "no-hire", "induce", "hire", "personnel/recruit/staff" and "non-compete/restrictive covenant" returned no hits anywhere in the document. Every occurrence of "employee"/"employ" is unrelated to restrictive covenants: the no-recourse-against-individuals clauses (p0244, p0284, quoted above), the "Indemnified Person" definition in the Servicer indemnity (p0291), the ERISA/Benefit Plan definitions (p0649, p0651, p0740), and the Independent Manager eligibility definition (p0770). Article VII (Servicer Resignation and Termination; Successor Servicer) — the provision where a servicing-transfer employee restriction would typically sit — likewise contains no such language.

This meets the preferred position ("No non-solicit on Customer") in full, so the fallback's narrowing elements (mutuality, personnel directly involved, 12-month tail, general-advertisement and unsolicited-approach carve-outs, no no-hire) are not reached. The absence of any restriction operates entirely in our favour and is not redlined; no elementCoverage is mapped because a compliant finding proposes no operation and the preferred element is satisfied by the absence of clause text rather than by any quotable provision. No action required.
